page.layout: One page of text, one column; running head at top; catchword-like signature "H gens" at foot right, with "gens" as a catchword below the last line.

main_text.p: & magis ramofarum particularum lactis, quæ anteà divisæ fero innatabant, unde partes illæ ramosæ sibi adhærefcunt, earumque concretione sive coagulatione postea fit caseus, ex viridissimâ autem illâ coagulatâ massâ sive caseo, cui ovillorum stercorum tinctura intricata est, serum subalbidum profluit; nec aliam novi rationem quare Hippocrates Aphor: 72. Sect: iv. & alibi sæpè toties monet, nalum signum esse cum phreneticorum & melancholicorum urinæ pellucidæ sunt & albæ; quam quia bilis sanguinis ramosis particulis potius adhæret; sero pariter à salsi & acidi acrimoniâ crassiore reddito. quod, quia tum à sanguinis particulis rubicundis sive magis ramosis separatur; ut solitò plus mingatur, uti non semel in phreniticis observavi, unde sanguis duplici de causâ justo calidior & acrior redditus phrenesim producere potest: Ciniflones certè chymici gens

page.notes: Printed lines are partly damaged at the left edge; the left-hand letters of many lines are cut off by the scan and have been reconstructed as far as legible. The word "gens" at the foot is a catchword; "H" is a signature mark. Words such as "lactis", "ramosæ" and "subalbidum" are read with some doubt.
